questions.question_text: Coded syllogism. Definitions: M % N means no M is N; M @ N means all M are N; M & N means some M are N; M © N means some M are not N; M $ N means only a few M are N; M # N means some M are N is a possibility; M ^ N means some M are not N is a possibility. Statement: Dream & experience $ happy & horrible. Conclusions: I. Dream # horrible. II. Experience & horrible.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: The coded statement guarantees some Dream are Experience, only a few Experience are happy, and some happy are horrible. It does not force Experience to overlap horrible; Dream–horrible overlap remains possible under the stated relations, so only I follows.

questions.question_text: Reverse syllogism. Given conclusions: I. No water being ice is a possibility. II. Some tea are drink. Choose the statement set that makes both conclusions follow.

options.A: All ice are tea. All drink is ice. No tea is a Pepsi. No Pepsi is a water.
options.B: Some ice are not tea. Some drinks are not ice. Some tea are not Pepsi. No Pepsi is a water.
options.C: All ice is tea. Some drinks are ice. Some tea are Pepsi. All Pepsi are water.
options.D: Some ice are tea. All drinks are ice. No tea is a Pepsi. All Pepsi are water.
options.E: Some ice are tea. All drinks are ice. Some tea is Pepsi. No Pepsi is water.

questions.explanation: Option C says all ice are tea and some drinks are ice; therefore some tea are drink. It places no restriction that forces water to overlap ice, so their non-overlap remains possible. The other sets do not establish both conclusions.

questions.question_text: Reverse syllogism. Given conclusions: I. Some iron are not metals. II. Some aluminium are not metals. Choose the statement set that makes both conclusions follow.

options.A: All metal are iron. Some metal are aluminium. No pot is metal.
options.B: No metal is iron. Some iron are pots. No pot is aluminium.
options.C: All metals are iron. Some iron are pots. No pot is aluminium.
options.D: No metal is iron. Some iron are pots. All pot is aluminium.
options.E: All metals are steel. Some iron are metals. No pot is aluminium.

questions.explanation: Option D gives some iron that are pots and states no metal is iron, so that existing iron is not metal. All pots are aluminium, making that same existing iron also aluminium and not metal; both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text: Q31. Statements: A few Fruit are Orange. Many Orange are Apple. Some Apple are Mango. Conclusions: I. Some Fruit are not Apple is a possibility. II. Some Orange are not Mango.
questions.explanation: The statements do not force every fruit-orange overlap into Apple, so a fruit outside Apple is possible and I follows as a possibility. No statement guarantees an orange outside Mango, so II does not follow.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 9, Q31

questions.question_text: Q32. Statements: All rats are bats. Only a few bats are cats. Conclusions: I. Some rats cannot be cats (possibility of rats outside cats). II. Some bats are not cats.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.B: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: ‘Only a few bats are cats’ guarantees some bats outside cats, so II follows. Rats are a subset of bats and may occupy the non-cat region; the source’s ‘can not’ possibility wording makes I possible as well. Both follow.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 10, Q32

questions.question_text: Q33. Statements: A few neighbours are good. All good are boys. Some boys are cool. Conclusions: I. A few neighbours cannot be cool (possibility). II. Some cool are not good.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.B: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: The statements do not force neighbours to overlap cool, so some of the neighbour group can be outside cool; I is possible. The existing cool boys could all be good, so II is not definite.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 11, Q33

questions.question_text: Q34. Statements: Only a few windows are gates. Some doors are windows. No rod is a gate. Conclusions: I. Some window cannot be rod. II. Some rod are not window.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.B: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: Only a few windows are gates guarantees some window-gates. Since no rod is a gate, those windows cannot be rods, establishing I. Nothing establishes existence of a rod outside windows, so II does not follow.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 12, Q34

questions.question_text: Q35. Statements: No plant is a bird. Some birds are cats. Only cats are dogs. Conclusions: I. Some cats can be not birds. II. Very few plants are not birds.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.B: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: The bird-cat existence does not prevent additional cats outside birds, so I is possible. No plant is a bird makes any plants non-birds, but plant existence is not given, so the existential ‘very few’ conclusion II does not follow.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 13, Q35

questions.question_text: Q36. Statements: Some ships are boats. All boats are submarines. Only submarines are planes. Conclusions: I. Some ships not being planes is a possibility. II. All ships are not planes.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.B: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: Some ships are submarines, but no statement forces ships to be planes; placing the existing ship-boat outside planes is possible, so I follows. The universal claim that all ships are not planes is not established.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 14, Q36

questions.question_text: Q43. Statements: Every A is B. All B are C. Only a few D are C. Conclusions: I. All C which are D cannot be A. II. Some D are not B.
questions.explanation: Only a few D are C ensures some D lie outside C; since B is within C, those D are not B, so II follows. The D∩C portion is not forced outside A, so I does not follow.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 15, Q43

questions.question_text: Q44. Statements: All cats are dogs. Only a few dogs are deer. At least a few deer are goats. Conclusions: I. All goats are dogs. II. Some deer are cats.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: The deer-goat existence does not force goats into dogs. The dog-deer overlap guaranteed by ‘only a few’ does not require cats to exist or overlap deer. Neither conclusion follows.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 16, Q44

questions.question_text: Q45. Statements: All pens are pencils. No pencil is a book. Only a few books are copies. Conclusions: I. Some pens are books. II. Some copies are not pencils.

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: I contradicts the separation of pencils and books. ‘Only a few books are copies’ guarantees some book-copy overlap; since no pencil is a book, those copies are not pencils, so II follows.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 17, Q45

questions.question_text: Q47. Statements: Only a few pets are cats. All bats are pets. Conclusions: I. Some pets are not cats. II. Some bats are cats.

options.C: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.D: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: Only a few pets are cats guarantees some pets outside cats, so I follows. Bats are only known to be pets; their overlap with cats is not required, so II does not follow.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 19, Q47

questions.question_text: Q48. Statements: Only a few wood are tables. Almost all tables are chairs. All chairs are desks. Conclusions: I. Some tables are desks. II. Some chairs are wood.

options.C: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.D: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.explanation: ‘Almost all tables are chairs’ guarantees some table-chair members; all chairs are desks, so I follows. The wood-table members are not guaranteed to lie in the chair portion, so II is not forced.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 20, Q48

questions.question_text: Q49. Statements: Occasionally C are D. No C is E. All E are F. Conclusions: I. No F is C. II. At least some D are F.

options.A: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.B: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.E: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: C and D overlap, but F can overlap C outside E because only E is excluded from C; thus I is not forced. The C-D overlap need not intersect F, so II is not forced. Neither follows.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 21, Q49

questions.question_text: Q50. Statements: Every ant is red. A few red are black. Only black is cat. Conclusions: I. Some cats are ants. II. No cat is an ant.
questions.explanation: Cats are within black, while ants are within red. The overlap of ant and cat is not specified; neither a nonempty overlap nor a complete separation is forced. Neither conclusion follows.
questions.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 22, Q50
